target_customer: Cell therapy developers, biopharma manufacturers and researchers who need to deliver DNA, RNA or other charged molecules into cells
problem: Conventional electroporation damages cells, can arc and is hard to scale, while viral delivery has its own limits. Sigma uses pulsed magnetic fields to deliver molecules non-invasively.
business_model: Hardware devices (Magnetoporator platform) and likely partnerships and grant-funded development; pricing not found
product_category: Cell engineering and gene delivery devices

founders.name: Karen Eaton
founders.background_notes: YC page: business skills with a scientific background; interests in cell and gene therapy.

founders.name: Matthew Scholz
previous_startups: Five biotechnology companies founded or co-founded (names not given on the YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC page: serial entrepreneur in gene therapy and computer security with dozens of patents.

founders.name: Chris Pihl
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; no background given.

technical_complexity.rationale: Novel physical gene delivery hardware needing biophysics, device engineering and biological validation with a two person team.

defensibility.rationale: A patent portfolio is reported (5 patents per Patsnap) but magnetofection is a known method category, so differentiation depends on device performance.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copycat move found as of search.

market_need_then: Cell and gene therapy were growing quickly in 2017 and viral and electroporation delivery were recognized bottlenecks, but no dated source was opened to quantify demand.

branding.domain_note: sigmagenetics.com; the live site was only a Coming Soon placeholder with a Bluehost template at fetch time.

brand_strength.rationale: Placeholder website, no press about the brand, and the name is easily confused with Sigma-Aldrich results.

outcome_analysis: Sigma Genetics entered YC in W17 with a magnetic-field gene delivery device and remains listed as active. Aggregator and bio data suggest roughly 3.5M raised including about 1.7M of non-dilutive money from the Andy Hill CARE Fund and the US Department of Defense, with partners including Seattle Children's. The company has stayed small and slow in a long-cycle hardware niche, and no exit or failure evidence was found.
notes: Funding totals are unverified aggregator or bio claims: about 3.5M to 3.74M total including 1.67M to 1.73M non-dilutive (Andy Hill CARE Fund, DoD), latest round dated 2026 by CB Insights and Caplight with conflicting types. No round is recorded. Crunchbase lists Scholz and Pihl as founders and other directories list Eaton, so only the YC page trio is listed. The website at fetch time was a Coming Soon placeholder, which may mean a dead or parked domain while other sources describe an active company. Competitor list empty: only general magnetofection overviews were found, none dated near 2017. Founded 2016 per directories.
